title: Operation of the Inspection Clock on a Live Keyturn Vehicle Listing
content:
Every live vehicle carries an inspection clock that runs on two dimensions at once, miles and days, and whichever falls due first is the one that governs.

**Clause withdrawn.** "A completed inspection grants the class's mileage interval afresh and sets the next due date the class's day interval ahead, counted in whole calendar days from the day of the inspection." That clause is no longer in force on a Keyturn Vehicle Listing and is not to be applied; what a completed inspection grants is settled on the current basis for the interval a completed inspection grants. The class intervals themselves keep their standing and are still the figures the clock runs on.

Odometer readings consume the interval as they are recorded, whether they come from a trip handover, from telematics or from the host's own periodic reading, and the host must report a reading at least once in the class's reporting interval even where the vehicle has taken no trips.

**Clause withdrawn.** "A telematics reading is authoritative where one exists; a host reading standing more than the class's variance tolerance away from the telematics figure is queried rather than recorded, and the listing is not suspended while the query is open." That clause is no longer in force on a Keyturn Vehicle Listing and is not to be applied; a host's reading is now dealt with on the current basis for the miles a reading the host reports takes off the interval. The class variance tolerance keeps its standing as a published figure of the class.

A vehicle past its interval may continue to take trips through the class's mileage and day grace, and is suspended once both the interval and the grace have been overrun; the grace is not a second interval and cannot be granted twice.

A failed inspection suspends the listing at once whatever the grace says, and the vehicle returns only after a re-inspection passes, for which the class's re-inspection fee is charged.

### When a record may be written at all

Records are written only while the listing is in the listed, snoozed or suspended state, since a draft vehicle has no clock running and a delisted one has none left. The standing is read off the marketplace's own record of the listing before the record is written, and is gathered to the vehicle by the listing the record is written against.

| Standing of the listing | An inspection or odometer record may be written |
| --- | --- |
| draft | no |
| under review | no |
| live | yes |
| snoozed | yes |
| suspended | yes |
| taken down for good | no |

superseded_clauses: A completed inspection grants the class's mileage interval afresh and sets the next due date the class's day interval ahead, counted in whole calendar days from the day of the inspection.

A telematics reading is authoritative where one exists; a host reading standing more than the class's variance tolerance away from the telematics figure is queried rather than recorded, and the listing is not suspended while the query is open.
